Answer: B
Reason: Comparing Figure 1 to Figure 4, the tubular opacity (bronchocele) in the left upper lobe appears relatively stable or slightly more defined, but the surrounding hyperlucent area (representing air trapping/hyperinflation typical of bronchial atresia) has become more prominent and larger in Figure 4. This progression is characteristic of congenital bronchial atresia where the distal lung segment becomes hyperinflated over time.
